meta.fx_note: All AUM/earnings in USD. FRE = Fee-Related Earnings. DE = Distributable Earnings. SRE = Spread-Related Earnings. PII = Principal Investment Income.

executive_read: Fee-related earnings quality is diverging from headline AUM growth. The names compounding fee-paying AUM on perpetual capital — ARES, OWL — carry premium EV/FRE multiples that are increasingly defensible; the names leaning on episodic realisations and carry — CG, TPG — trade cheap for a reason. The structural story remains the migration of credit and insurance balance sheets onto alt-AM platforms: APO and KKR are now as much spread businesses as fee businesses, and that is where the next leg of earnings durability is being built. Watch SBC creep at ARES, where stock comp is inflating reported FRE margin faster than peers, and watch the wealth channel, where redemption queues are normalising everywhere except OWL.
bottom_line: On a quality-adjusted basis we would rank the group: perpetual-capital compounders (ARES, OWL) and insurance-levered platforms (APO, KKR) ahead of realisation-dependent managers (CG, TPG). Valuation already reflects much of this — the mispricing, if any, sits in CG trading below closed-deal takeout comps while carrying the lowest earnings quality, a classic value-trap signature rather than a clean entry. This is an analytical judgement, not a recommendation.
